newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM rules out new IMF stand-by accord--paper.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM rules out new IMF stand-by accord--paper.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has ruled out any stand-by agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which is holding talks with officials on the economy, he was quoted on Friday as saying.
"We do not need to sign a new stand-by agreement with the IMF, but of course we would still like the IMF to present a positive report," he told the mass-circulation Milliyet daily.
He said his Islamist-led government might issue a new currency to replace the Turkish lira which would be "in equal value with foreign currencies", but did not elaborate.
Turkey's draft 1997 budget, partly announced by the government on Thursday, would have a zero deficit thanks to the "ample resources of the country", Erbakan said.

The budget envisages spending of 6,200 trillion lira and 4,300 trillion lira of tax revenues expected from two sets of measures announced in the past two months to raise resources to close fiscal and trade deficits.
The budget is expected to bring in non-tax revenues worth 1,420 trillion lira and 420 trillion lira from privatisations.
The 1997 budget draft was presented to parliament for debate late on Thursday night.
Erbakan said the government would continue paying its domestic and foreign debts in 1997, but did not give details.
